patch_description: This approach builds a demand-informed diffusion model rather than scoring links primarily by their individual traffic. It estimates which relays can usefully connect high-demand source–destination pairs, then rewards corresponding two-link wedges with a capacity-discounted benefit. A separate positive interaction discourages selecting pairs of links that concentrate traffic on an already high-pressure receiver. The construction uses only linear terms and O(n³) quadratic terms, and uses mean incident demand to measure relay pressure.
